title: 7% Flat = 13% Real? The Car Loan Trick Nobody Shows You
description:
Your car dealer says 7% flat. The real rate is 13%. Here is the math nobody shows you.

5 lakh loan, 5 years, 7% flat = 1,75,000 interest (EMI 11,250). A 13% reducing-balance loan costs the SAME. Quick rule: multiply any flat rate by 1.8 to get the real rate. Always ask for the reducing balance rate or APR.

Follow Market Debunk - we read the fine print so you don't have to. Share this with someone buying a car this year.

#MarketDebunk #CarLoan #PersonalFinance #India #MoneyTips
beats: Seven percent flat means thirteen percent real. Here is the math nobody shows you.
Arun is buying his first car. The salesman smiles and says: loan at just seven percent flat. Sounds like a steal.
Here is the trick. Flat rate means you pay interest on the full five lakhs, for all five years. Even after you have repaid most of it.

Five lakh loan, five years, seven percent flat: interest comes to one lakh seventy-five thousand. E-M-I eleven thousand two fifty. Now get this - a thirteen percent reducing loan costs exactly the same.
So that seven percent flat? It is really thirteen percent in disguise. Quick rule: multiply any flat rate by one point eight.
What do you do? Always ask one question: what is the reducing balance rate, or the A-P-R? Compare that number, never the flat one.
Flat rate versus reducing balance. Two small words, one lakh difference. Now you know which one to ask for.
